v: Know the job of a design
Spot why some posters look professional and others do not

b.v: About 20 minutes. Any free design app on your phone or computer is fine for this course.

A design is not decoration. Its job is to make one message clear in a few seconds: 'Sale this Friday', 'We fix phones', 'Join our class'. If people cannot tell the message in 3 seconds, the design has failed, however pretty it is.

v: Too many fonts and colours
Everything is the same size, so nothing stands out
Text squeezed to the edges
Blurry or stretched pictures

b.v: Step by step:|Show your design to someone for 3 seconds.|Take it away.|Ask: what was it about? If they cannot say, simplify it.
Do this now:|Collect 5 posters or posts you like and 5 you dislike.|Write one reason for each.|Keep this collection - it is your 'inspiration folder'.

v: Use empty space on purpose
Line things up
Make the most important thing biggest

b.v: Empty space is not wasted space. It gives the eye a rest and makes the message stand out. Leave a clear margin around the edges - at least the width of your thumb on a phone-sized design.
Line up text and pictures along invisible lines - all left, or all centred. When elements are placed randomly the design feels messy even if the viewer cannot say why.

v: 1st - the big message (headline)
2nd - the key detail (date, price, offer)
3rd - the small print (address, phone, website)

b.v: Squint at your design. Whatever you still see clearly is what people notice first.
Do this now:|Make a post for 'Free eye check-up, Saturday 10am-2pm'.|Make the headline 3 times bigger than the details.|Align everything to the left and keep a margin.

v: Choose a colour palette
Keep text readable
1 main colour - your brand colour
1 accent colour - for buttons, prices and highlights
Neutrals - white, light grey, dark grey or near-black for text
Green - fresh, natural, money, Islamic themes
Blue - trust, calm, banks, tech
Red and orange - energy, food, sale, urgency
Black and gold - luxury, weddings

b.v: Text must stand out from its background: dark text on light, or light text on dark. Yellow text on white or red text on green is hard to read, especially for older people.
Never put text directly on a busy photo. Add a solid or semi-transparent band behind it.
Do this now:|Choose a main and an accent colour for a real or imaginary business.|Redo yesterday's post with these colours.|Check the text is easy to read on a phone at arm's length.

v: Pair two fonts
Write less text
One strong font for headlines
One simple, readable font for everything else
For Urdu, a clean Nastaliq or Naskh font - and never stretch it

b.v: People do not read posters - they glance at them. Cut your text in half, then cut it again. Keep the headline under 7 words if you can.

v: No ALL CAPITALS for long sentences
Do not centre long paragraphs
Keep line spacing comfortable
Check spelling twice - especially names and phone numbers

b.v: Do this now:|Write a 30-word event announcement.|Cut it to 15 words without losing the meaning.|Design it with only two fonts.

v: Use sharp, legal pictures
Crop for focus
Use photos larger than your design, never enlarge small ones
Never stretch a photo out of shape - resize from a corner
One great photo beats five average ones

b.v: Crop away anything that does not help the message. Faces and products should fill the frame. Leave space in the direction a person is looking.

v: Your own photos - best for real products
Free stock photo sites that allow commercial use - read the licence
Simple icons in one style, all outline or all filled

b.v: Pictures from a web search are usually owned by someone. Using them in a business design can bring a copyright complaint.
Do this now:|Take a photo of a product near a window.|Crop it three different ways.|Choose the crop that makes the product clearest.

v: Use the right sizes
Build a post template you can reuse
Square post - 1080 x 1080 pixels
Tall post - 1080 x 1350 pixels (shows bigger in feeds)
Story or short video cover - 1080 x 1920 pixels
Link preview / cover - 1200 x 630 pixels

b.v: In stories and short videos the top and bottom of the screen get covered by names, buttons and captions. Keep important text in the middle area.

v: Your logo always in the same corner
Same two fonts and colours
A fixed spot for the headline and the call to action
Change only the photo and words each time

b.v: A consistent look makes people recognise your posts before they read the name.
Do this now:|Make a 1080 x 1350 template with your logo, colours and fonts.|Use it for three different posts.|Put the three side by side - do they look like one brand?

v: Know what makes a logo work
Sketch and test logo ideas
Recognisable when tiny - on a phone or a pen
Works in one colour (black and white)
Not full of details or gradients
Fits the business: a law firm and a toy shop should not look the same
Wordmark - the name in a special style
Icon - a symbol
Combination - icon plus name, the most common for small businesses

b.v: Step by step:|Write 10 words that describe the business.|Sketch 10 tiny ideas on paper in 10 minutes - quantity first.|Pick 3 and make them on the computer in black only.|Test them very small and on a dark background.|Add colour last.
Never copy or slightly change another company's logo. It is illegal and can force the business to throw away all its printed material.
Do this now:|Do the 5-step process for a made-up business, for example 'Ali's Chai Corner'.

day-8.t: Day 8 — Print design: cards, flyers, banners

v: Prepare designs that print correctly
Avoid costly print mistakes
Use high resolution - 300 DPI for small prints like cards and flyers
Ask the printer for the exact size, including 'bleed' (extra 3 mm on each side that gets cut off)
Keep text at least 5 mm inside the cut line
Colours look darker on paper than on a bright phone screen
Name, title, phone, email or website, address
Logo
A QR code to your profile or digital card
Readable text - at least 8 point

b.v: Send printers a high-quality PDF, not a screenshot. Always ask for one test print before printing 1,000 copies.
XpertCreation's digital card (/c/yourname) works well as the QR code target on a printed card.
Do this now:|Design a visiting card at the standard size your printer uses, with bleed.|Add a QR code.|Print one copy at home or a shop and check it.

day-9.t: Day 9 — Feedback and fixing your own work

v: Review designs with a checklist
Take feedback without taking it personally
Can the message be understood in 3 seconds?
Is one thing clearly the most important?
Two fonts, a small palette?
Enough space and good alignment?
Readable on a phone?
Spelling, phone number and dates correct?

b.v: Do not ask 'Do you like it?'. Ask 'What do you notice first?' and 'What would you do after seeing this?'. The answers show whether the design works.

v: Agree how many rounds of changes are included before you start
Ask why a change is wanted - the real problem may need a different fix
Save each version so you can go back

b.v: Do this now:|Run the checklist on everything you made this week.|Fix one design.|Show the before and after to a friend.

v: Make a small brand kit for one business
Share it as a portfolio piece
Logo in colour and in black
Colour palette with codes
Two fonts
One social post template
One visiting card

b.v: Show the kit on one image: logo at the top, colours as circles, fonts written out, then the post and the card. Write 3 lines: the business, the problem, your solution.
